newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Index-linked funds propel Brussels bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Index-linked funds propel Brussels bourse higher.

text.p: Good news on U.S. inflation and banks covering the launch of index-linked investment funds combined to propel Belgium's Bel-20 leading share index to new heights on Thursday, dealers said.

The decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve on Wednesday to leave its interest rates unchanged and the U.S. June employment report on Thursday which showed little or no wage pressures in the economy were greeted by a worldwide surge in equity prices.
Traders said in Belgium the movement got an added boost from new cash from index-linked funds launched by banks Generale Bank and Kredietbank earlier this week.
Subscriptions to Kredietbank's "Bel-20 Premium 1" fund are not due to close until July 25.
"You can see it every day between two and three (in the afternoon) when all the prices get hit," one trader said, referring to the time when the funds' starting-levels against the index are fixed.
The Bel-20 ended up 1.76 percent at 2,488.07 points, with 17 of its 20 components firmly higher.

One trader said the wave of optimism helped lift stocks which had underperformed recently, such as chemicals company Solvay, which rose 4.23 percent to 22,775 francs despite news of a broker's downgrade early in the session.
Dollar-senstive metals company Union Miniere, downgraded on Wednesday, rose 5.22 percent.
Outside the Bel-20, construction and dredging firm CFE was the star performer, adding 9.27 percent to 11,200 francs.

In an investor note dated June 30, Antwerp brokerage Corluy & Co rated the share a 'buy', noting dredging unit DEME expected 1997 sales to grow by more than 50 percent to 23 billion francs. Corluy estimated DEME's value to CFE to be five billion francs compared with a market capitalisation of six billion.
CFE shares DEME with Belgian holding company Ackermans & Van Haaren, which ended 30 francs higher at 8,160. DEME's impact on AvH was much less, Corluy noted.
In a note published after the close, Belgium's Generale Bank also said it had raised CFE to a "buy". The share could hit 14,250 francs with ease, still 21 percent over Thursday's close, it said.
